newsitem.title: HONG KONG: The worst of Hong Kong fires.
newsitem.headline: The worst of Hong Kong fires.

text.p: The blaze that engulfed a Hong Kong building this week was the worst in a building on record in the British colony, but not the first fire to claim many lives. Here is a list of major fires in the colony's history.

1918 - In the worst fire on record, an estimated 600 people were killed and 400 injured at the Happy Valley racecourse on Hong Kong Island on the Lunar New Year holiday when a grandstand collapsed and food stall stoves were knocked over, setting bamboo matting ablaze.
1929 - A blaze in the Prince Edward Hotel in Hong Kong's Island's Central district kills nine people
1947 - The Canton steamer S.S. Sai On was consumed by fire on the Hong Kong dockside, killing 149 people.

1953 - On Christmas Day, the Shek Pik Mei squatter village fire burned down, making more than 60,000 homeless. There were no records of the exact numbers living there and the death toll is unknown. As a result of the fire, Hong Kong launched a drive to elimiate squatting by building cheap public housing, in which 3.5 million people now live.
1971 - Fire swept through the Jumbo Restaurant in Aberdeen harbour, killing 13 and injuring 42.
1972 - The cruise liner Queen Elizabeth, which was being used as a floating university, burned and sank in Hong Kong harbour with no casualties.
1981 - Eleven workers died in North Point wig factory fire.
1984 - Blaze raged through the Blue Box Industrial Building in Hing Wo Street, injuring 44.
1986 - Fire gutted Chu Ku Tsai village on Chinese Lunar New Year holiday, leaving 2,000 homeless.
1986 - Fourteen people were killed in a blaze at a garment factory in the Kwai Chung port district.
1986 - A Christmas blaze gutted 150 vessels moored in Aberdeen typhoon shelter on Hong Kong Island, leaving more than 1,700 boat dwellers homeless and virtually penniless. But only two were injured.
1990 - Triad gangsters fire-bombed a restaurant and majong parlour in Hunghom, killing six and injuring 24.
1990 - Six people were killed and 50 injured in a fire in a "cage home" slum hostel in Shamshuipo.
1992 - A blaze at the Shek Kong Vietnamese refugee detention centre killed 26 and injured 126.
1994 - A fire-bomb at the Shek Pik Mei branch of a Hong Kong bank killed 12 bank employees.
1996 - A February dry season brush fire traps schoolchildren hiking at Pat Sin Leng in the New Territories. Three pupils and two teachers killed, many suffer life-lasting burn injuries.
1996 - On November 20, the Garley Building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping street turns into a towering inferno, killing 39 people and injuring 81.
